messages:
maya: quick q — who actually owns the 'canary_traffic' feature flag vs the rollout policy in console? product flipped the flag but console still enforced the policy guards :thinking:
raj: i thought rollout policies should own traffic splits, flags are for app-level gating / feature toggles
theo: current runtime reads flags first then applies rollout policy overrides. awkward and leads to surprises
linh: yeah — we just had a customer where policy had a 5% canary but flag=true for all users -> canary never happened
maya: exactly the bug. can we define a simple precedence rule? my vote: rollout policy is authoritative for routing/traffic, flags only affect behavior after routing
raj: +1 on clarity. also need RBAC: product edits flags, platform edits policies. right now anyone with console access can edit both
pm-sara: product teams expect to run experiments (A/B) by toggling flags without platform involvement
theo: proposal from runtime side: 1) policy trumps traffic-related config (splits, guards). 2) flags evaluated after routing decisions. 3) console surfaces conflicts and owners
maya: quick sketch of schema we talked about:
```yaml
rollout_policy:
  id: rp-7
  traffic_split:
    model-a: 95
    model-b: 5
feature_flags:
  canary_model_b: true
```
theo: with the rule above model_b only gets 5% of traffic even if canary_model_b=true
linh: runtime should also return a clear conflict code when a flag would cause traffic leakage (eg 409 + "flag conflicts with rollout policy")
deploy-bot: deploy rp-7 -> success (3 nodes). warnings: conflict detected with feature flag canary_model_b (owned by product)
raj: what about legit cases where product *wants* control over traffic percentages? they'll be annoyed if platform always overrides
maya: we can add a policy field: "delegated: true" which explicitly hands traffic control to feature flags for that route/experiment
pm-sara: that would make product happy. they'd toggle delegated mode for experiments only
theo: implementable: add boolean in policy schema, runtime precedence check, and console UX change. small API bump but straightforward
linh: also require audit log entry + email alert when delegation flips (security / compliance)
maya: ok i'll write an RFC: include schema change, RBAC matrix, console mock, runtime precedence table, error codes, and migration plan
raj: sgtm. timeline?
maya: RFC draft by EOD Wednesday, will ping @theo for schema bits and @linh for audit hooks
theo: i'll add runtime checks + unit tests once RFC lands
pm-sara: i'll coordinate with experiment owners so they know the delegated pattern
maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
